task.description: Review the diff for REQ-001b (git diff master...HEAD on branch feature/WF02-REQ-001b, note: master here is REQ-001a's already-merged state) per WF-02 Step 2b. FRONTEND-DEV reported 2 MINOR deviations in its handoff (handoffs/WF02-REQ-001b/step-02-frontend-dev.json result.issues) — read them and judge on merits: (1) the design's key table didn't spell out exact key names for some of the 6 repeated-shape arrays, FRONTEND-DEV chose a consistent naming convention itself; (2) Streams' brand/URL text was extracted as a key per the design table's literal listing even though arguably a pass-through candidate. Also independently verify FRONTEND-DEV's own key claims: it reports 177 matching keys in both messages/ru.json and messages/uz.json — verify this yourself (a node script diffing the key sets, or similar) rather than trusting the number. Check the diff against docs/agents/anti-patterns.md (note: it now has one entry, about a result.status field-confusion mistake earlier in this same run — confirm this run's REVIEWER-facing handoff doesn't repeat that mistake, i.e. check your OWN result.status will be a legal value before you write it, not something you need to check in FRONTEND-DEV's diff). Check scope: copy-extraction only, no new components, no CSS changes, no anchor/href changes. Verify the two t.rich() emphasis calls (Hero.tsx, Creed.tsx) render correctly and use next-intl's real documented API, not an invented pattern.
acceptance_criteria: git diff master...HEAD read directly across all 14 changed files (12 components + 2 catalogs), not just the FRONTEND-DEV handoff summary
Independently verify the 177/177 matching-key-set claim with your own script/command
Both reported deviations explicitly judged, not silently accepted
Scope check confirms copy-extraction only, nothing else bundled in

result.summary: Read git diff master...HEAD directly and fully for all 14 in-scope files (12 landing components + messages/ru.json + messages/uz.json). Independently verified the 177/177 matching-key-set claim with a standalone node script (not trusting FRONTEND-DEV's number): flattened both catalogs' key sets, found ru key count 177, uz key count 177, zero keys only in ru, zero keys only in uz, zero empty uz values -- claim confirmed exactly. Judged both reported deviations on their merits: (1) the flat indexed key names FRONTEND-DEV chose for MapSection.CHAPTERS/Streams.STREAMS/Metrics.METRICS (chapterNName/chapterNDesc/chapterNStatus, streamNStatus/streamNTitle/streamNDesc, metricNLabel/metricNSource) are internally consistent with the talkNWho/teamNName indexed-key pattern the design table spelled out explicitly for Events/Team and that CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR confirmed as the resolved direction (design doc SS4 open question 4) -- not a violation, a defensible and predictable naming convention, and every key resolves 1:1 against the catalog (confirmed by the same script plus direct diff reading); (2) Streams' foundationTitle/foundationLink extraction is not an improvisation -- the design doc's own SS2 table (line naming Streams.tsx's keys) explicitly lists foundationTitle, foundationBody, and foundationLink as catalog keys, so FRONTEND-DEV followed the design's authoritative table literally rather than silently overriding it with its own brand-literal judgment call; the design team's deliberate distinction is visible elsewhere in the same diff (Nav/Footer 'AI Qadam' brand text and Footer's bare-domain ecosystem links, e.g. build.aiqadam.org as a Footer nav link, correctly remain untouched literals, and Partners.PARTNERS's proper-noun name field was also correctly left as a literal in the .tsx data, not extracted) -- confirming the codebase is not indiscriminately extracting every brand-adjacent string, only what the design table named. Both deviations are genuine, defensible judgment calls, not violations -- no rework needed. Verified both t.rich() calls (Hero.tsx title, Creed.tsx quote) against use-intl's actual shipped type definitions (node_modules/use-intl/dist/types/core/createTranslator.d.ts and createBaseTranslator.d.ts): `rich` is a real, typed member of the Translator interface with signature `rich(key, values?: RichTranslationValues, formats?, _fallback?) => ReactNode`, and the diff's usage (`t.rich("quote", { em: (chunks) => {chunks} })`, same shape for Hero's "title") matches this signature exactly -- not invented syntax. Ran npm run build (exit 0, clean TypeScript + static generation), then npm run start and curled /ru and /uz directly: both responses contain literal `вместе.` and `не про искусственный интеллект.` tags, confirming t.rich() renders real markup (not escaped/literal) on both locales; server log showed no MISSING_MESSAGE/IntlError markers. Scope check: git diff --name-only confirms no .css/.scss files touched anywhere in the 14-file diff; grepped every added/removed href= line across the component diff and confirmed every href value is byte-identical before and after (only the anchor's visible text/children changed to t() calls) -- no anchor/component/CSS changes bundled in, copy-extraction only. Design-system compliance is trivially satisfied since no CSS was touched (confirmed above) and no visual/token changes are possible from a translation-call substitution. Checked docs/agents/anti-patterns.md's one entry (result.status field-confusion from step-01) before writing this handoff's own result.status -- set to the legal value 'PASS' (not 'COMPLETED', which is the separate lifecycle status field, itself correctly set to 'COMPLETED' above) per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's PASS|FAIL|PARTIAL|BLOCKED|SKIPPED table.

issues.description: FRONTEND-DEV's naming-convention judgment call for MapSection/Streams/Metrics indexed array keys (chapterNName/streamNTitle/metricNLabel style) is sound and internally consistent with the design-confirmed talkNWho/teamNName pattern, but the design doc itself never spelled these exact names out -- future designs for repeated-shape arrays should name every key explicitly in the SS2 table (as was done for Events/Team) to remove this class of judgment call at the design stage rather than the implementation stage.

Streams.foundationTitle/foundationLink extraction is a defensible literal reading of the design's SS2 table, but the design doc's own open questions (SS4, brand/URL pass-through judgment calls) did not explicitly reconcile this against the non-copy-value rule for the six repeated-shape arrays' sibling non-array keys -- non-blocking, since the design table is authoritative and was followed as written, but worth CODE-DESIGNER double-checking brand/URL-adjacent keys against the non-copy-value rule before finalizing future SS2 tables.
